newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fernz defends management of interferon.
newsitem.headline: Fernz defends management of interferon.

text.p: Fernz Corp Ltd Managing Director Kerry Hoggard on Thursday defended the management of its low-dose oral interferon project against broker criticism.

Hoggard told the annual meeting that creating and perfecting the technology, achieving patent protection, developing registration, establishing distribution and marketing agreements and clinical research were all factors that did not appear as positives on the bottom line.

"It has therefore been difficult for the share market to recognise the value that the board and management believe is in the project," he said. "Some analysts have also expressed concerns on the managerial skills we have in the company to conduct business in this sector," he said.
Hoggard said there were three key elements.
The first was that Fernz had demonstrated it had the technical skill to produce an international-quality product and had achieved international patents.

Secondly, he believed Fernz had the skill to register the product, having already done so in 77 countries with agricultural chemical products. Procedures differed little for animal and human health registrations, he added.
Thirdly, in the pharmaceuticals market, the company did not have the skills to market the project internationally and nor did it intend to.
"This will be completed by agreement with specialists in this business sector around the world," he said.

The interferon project made a NZ$5.0 million loss in the year to May 1996. This was forecast to narrow to a NZ$1.9 million loss in 1997, turning to a $1.2 million profit in 1998 and a $5.3 million profit in 1999.
Hoggard said Fernz expected the product to be in use in 10 countries in the years to come, thus reducing its reliance on its main customer, China.
